I understand too, that in the case of this shed we will charge a certain amount on the goods that will be stored there-that is the understanding. Unfortunately I have not got the details as to which will be charged. As I say, there is no established tariff in regard to these wharves;

it depends upon the circumstances, the importance of the locality, and the extent of the traffic. In the present instance the venture is practically a new one necessitated by the development which has taken place at Cap de la Madeleine.

Will the wharfinger be
appointed there?
Yes.

Item agreed to.
Caughnawaga-wharf reconstruction, $8,000.

We spent $2,500 last
year to repair this wharf, and this year we are going to spend $8,000 to reconstruct it.

This is another
section of the wharf. There is tremendous traffic passing across the river at that point, and boats are running hourly or oftener. Last year over 31,178 automobiles crossed at this point, 3,279 trucks and 2,233 other vehicles. It is estimated that the traffic will amount to about 45,000 vehicles.
Hoiw much do they pay?

It is a private
feny company.

How much does each
vehicle pay for landing on the wharf?
Nothing.
Is there a ferry across the river?
'Yes.
Will this complete the programme at this point?
Yes.
Is this to be by contract?
Yes, under contract.
Is it under contract?
We constructed a part of it last year. This is a new section which will be under contract this year.
Not yet under contract?
No.

Item agreed to.
Chateau Richer-wharf repairs, $1,450.
Where is this?

In Charlevoix-
Montmorency.

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

On. the St. Lawrence
river?
Yes.
How long has that wharf been there?

The wharf is 272
feet long and $34,000 has been expended.

Item agreed to.
Chicoutimi Basin-wharf repairs, $1,500.
This is not Charlevoix?

No, C'hicoutimi-
Saguenay.
Mr. STEVEN'S:	In 1923-24 there was an
item of $6,000 for this wharf, apparently all spent. In 1924-25 the amount was $4,800, and now we have an item of $1,500.

This is a large
structure and there are some repairs practically every year. Last year, 1924-25 we spent $4,686. The wharf is a very large one, and 1,200 passengers passed over the wharf last year, 350 vehicles and 100 tons of freight weekly. It is one of the terminal wharves on the Saguenay river.
There have been certainly very heavy repairs. In 1921-22, $6,000, in 1923-24, $6,000 and 1924-25, $4,800 was spent on repairs. It averages about $5,000. What is the revenue from this wharf?

The customs
revenue at that point?
No, the revenue from the wharf? Is there no wharfage at all?

Well, it is not
very great, it is a small collection. In 1923 the collections were $240 and in 1922, $145. The customs revenue was $67,455. There were 23 sea-going vessels and 99 coasting inland vessels. The ocean tons amounted to 38,264 and the coasting inland tonnage 121,000, making 159,000 tons.

Does it not strike the
minister and the government as an extraordinary position? Here is a wharf described as a very important one, and I have no doubt it is. We have spent $5,000 per year in repairing it alone, and we get one year $240 and another year $145 in revenue. I really think we ought to face the question of obtaining revenue at these places that are capable of paying considerable sums for the accommodation given to them. Can the minister hold out any hope that there will be
revenue from this wharf in the future? It rather destroys confidence in the suggestion that there will be revenue in the future on these new commitments. That is the point I desire to make.

The report we
had from the Marine department shows collections last year of some two hundred dollars odd, but I notice here that we have in 1921, 1922 and 1923 apparently collected revenues that are not shown on that sheet. In 1921 the figure is $4,928, in 1922, $5,638, and in 1923, $7,818. Those apparently are not customs collections.
Who collected them?
I think the Marine department.
I think the minister gave us the Marine department figures.
There seems to be some confusion, or else this is not a correct statement.
The Minister of Marine and Fisheries is in the chamber, and we would like to have these correct figures.
I do not think he would have them in his mind. I will be glad to advise my hon. friend later as to the correctness of these figures.
It would not be much good later, but it would be interesting.

It is a very small item. I do not think my hon. friend wishes to hold up the annual repairs to a structure of this kind. That is not the intention I understand, and I will be glad to verify the figures which I have given and which I hope are correct.
The next day the Minister of Marine and Fisheries is dealing with his estimates he might give the figures.

Has the minister ever had a census taken of the wharves in the eastern provinces? Does he know how many there are? I have been looking over the Auditor General's report and find page after page of wharves, and I think we should have a return of these wharves.
It is an expensive thing to take a census.

These wharves are visited by the departmental engineers each year.

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

Has the minister any
figures of the number of wharves in that province?
I have not them before me. Many wharves are shown in the items before us to-day, but many others do not appear. There is a complete list of these works in the department.

Item agreed to.
Contrecceur-wharf improvements, $1,100.
What is this item?
This is to improve the flooring by Laying a six-inch concrete flooring on 115 feet long of the right of way to wharf 17.6 feet wide.
When was it floored last?
What county is it in?
Chambly-Vercheres.
Floored before the last general election.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
speechtext: Did the right hon. member floor it for the last election?
It is a frank admission.

Item agreed to.
Coteau Landing-improvement to wharf approach
11.000.
What county is that in?

Vaudreuil county. This is required to complete the work let in 1024 and 1925 for repairing and improving the approach of this wharf. It consists of laying a concrete floor. Last year $1,739, was expended.

Item agreed to.
Cross Point-wharf extension, $5,000.
What county is this in?

Bonaventure.
There is a revote of $3,600. This is to complete the contract at that point.
Why was it all deferred to this year?

We spent $2,800
last year. This is to complete the work.

If the minister spent
$2,800 out of a vote of $3,600, how is there $3,600 left?

We are asking
for $5,000 now. There was nothing spent at the time the estimates were made up.
According to the estimates there was nothing spent last year. Now we are told that $2,800 is spent out of a vote of $3,600, the minister says that $3,600 still remains to be revoted.

There was $2,837
spent. We are asking for $5,000 of which $3,600 is a revote.

Either the minister is
twisted or the estimates are wrong.

Did the minister take
that out of the general vote?

When the estimates were .made up, we estimated that we would require $5,000 to complete the work. Since then the work proceeded and $2,837 was expended before March 31, 1925. We spent more than we thought we should, and therefore we shall not require the full estimate of $5,000. Of course these estimates were made up long before the 31st March.

The minister says that
$2,837 was spent.
Yes.
Before it was voted?
No. Out of last year's vote.

He cannot have spent it out oi last year's vote or his estimates are wrongly printed. I have made this statement several times and the minister does not seem to have got it yet. Last year's vote was $3,600. The .minister asks that of that $3,600, the whole of amount be revoted. He cannot have the whole amount if he has spent anything. So he cannot have spent any of last year's vote. Therefore, if he has spent $2,837, he has spent it out this year's vote before we have had the privilege of voting it.
No.
What is the explanation?

I thought I hau
made it plain that the $2,837 was spent out of last year's vote. My right hon. friend is confused. When our estimates were made up, we did not expect to expend any part of last year's appropriation and an estimate was made up of $5,000 to carry this expenditure. Of that amount, $3,600 would be a revote. In tne meantime, after the estimates had been made up and printed, the contractor went ahead and spent out of last year's vote some $2,837. We are not changing the vote. We will complete the contract and the

Supply-Harbours and Rivers
balance that is unexpended will lapse. The thing is perfectly clear. .

It is clear now, but
the minister did not make it clear before. The fact of the matter is that this revote is wrong. There is not $3,600 to be revoted.
That is true.

Item agreed to.
Desjardins-wharf reconstruction, $16,000.
Who gets this?

This is in the
county of Pontiac. It is for reconstruction of the wharf from the water line.
What river is it on?

The Ottawa river. The amount is required for the proper maintenance of this wharf in good repair, to accommodate a regular traffic, averaging 150 passengers, fifty rigs and fifteen automobiles daily. It is used by a number of farmers in the vicinity, and general supplies and merchandise pass over the wharf.
When was this reconstructed last?
I have not the date of the last reconstruction. Probably it was some years ago. There has been a total expenditure of $21,261 at this point.
That is all that has ever been spent there?
Yes.
How do the automobiles pass over?
They cross back and forth on tne river.
There is a ferry?
Yes.
What is the revenue from this wharf?
We do not operate the ferry. There is no revenue from the wharf.
Is the minister hopeful that with the reconstruction there will be a revenue?
Not at, that point.
Why?

Because of the character of the traffic, it would not probably be one of the points at which it is usuai to make a charge. I do not think the government has any desire to change its policy in that regard at the present time.
Do automobiles cross at this point?
They cross the river. They pay the charges for the ferry, but they do not pay for crossing the wharf.
Does the ferry company pay nothing?
They do not pay anything, to my knowledge.
Who makes a contract with the ferry?
We license them through the Public Works department. The fee is only a nominal one.
Who operates the ferry?
I have not the name of the individual operator. That would be available in the department if my hon. friend is interested.	.

Some
private concern.
Yes.
Is it customary to build these conveniences for private concerns for work of this kind without securing any work from them?

My hon. friend can hardly say that. This is a public wharf and it is a great public convenience. It is true that the ferry uses this wharf as it will the wharf on the other side of the river at Pembroke, Ontario. As for making a charge at this point, I do not think it is worth while. You would have to put somebody there to make your collections, and the work would cost more than the revenue collected.

I have in
mind the practice in some of the western provinces, where the provincial government installs the ferries and charges a fee after a certain hour at night. The people of the province pay for the service in that regard. Is it on a different 'basis in Ontario?
No.

Then why
does the federal government stjep, in and build the approaches? In Alberta the provincial government builds them. I have no doubt there is an explanation; what is it?

Supply-Harbours and Rivers
There is other traffic at this wharf.

There i3
also other traffic besides automobile traffic over the ferries in Alberta; for instance, there is a very heavy grain traffic both in summer and part of the winter.

Do you make a
charge for the use of the ferry?

After a
certain hour for the use of the ferry, not for the wharf.
Mr. KING (Kootenay) The government does not want to enter into the ferry business. That would be "worse and more of it."

The minister misunderstands me. In Alberta the government, though not in the ferry business, installs the ferries. In addition to that it builds the approaches and takes care of them. I want to find out what is the reason for the difference in Ontario in cases of this kind, where I find the federal government building the approaches for a private concern?

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
speechtext:
These are
not approaches, these are wharves where the steam ferries land.

Do boats
come up there and unload cargoes of merchandise?
Yes.

It is a
sort of port?
It is a "national port."

If the hon. member will
just get the significance of this: he ought always to have a wharf where there is a ferry.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
speechtext:
No, there
are ferries without -wharves on this river, just as in Alberta we land on the dirt.
It is too bad that the hon. member in whose riding this huge sum is being expended is not here to support it and to give us some information.
What information would my hon. friend like?

We would like to know
why it is that a business operation can be carried on at a government wharf upon which $16,000 is being expended for repairs and reconstruction in one year without any revenue 
at all to justify it. It is really an aggravated case. We have been pointing out to the minister several instances where a few hundred dollars is collected and there is an expenditure of a thousand dollars every year. Here we have a large expenditure of $16,000, with a regular private business being carried on, and no revenue in return. I again suggest to the minister that the time has arrived when the federal authorities should secure revenue, because we are enlarging this liability. I admit it is a growth over a long period of years; but we discussed this last year, and this year we are met by exactly the same statements, indicating no serious thought whatever on the part of the government of either stopping the expenditure or getting some compensating revenue for it. Again I say, it -would be very much better if we could have hadi some support for this vote from the member in whose constituency the expenditure is being made, to show why these rather extravagant repairs should be made merely to accommodate a free ferry.

My hon. friend
is not fair. This is a wharf on the Ottawa river handling general traffic. It is true that one of the conveniences the people have there is a ferry service between Pembroke, the adjoining town, and Desjardins. The people who are landed on the wharf use it from that ferry. Does my hon. friend for one moment suggest that we should appoint a wharfinger to exact toll from the passengers using that ferry? If that is the policy he would like this department to adopt, why did he not consider it when he was in office? But I do not think he would entertain it at all if he were in charge. The collection would be so small that the cost would be out of all proportion. There are larger centres where wharfingers are appointed, and proper collections made, but this is a country district, and I do not think it would be good policy to make a charge.

The minister puts up a straw man to knock down. I never suggested a wharfinger should be appointed to collect revenue. There -would be no difficulty whatever where a ferry is landing regularly to have a small fee collected, either from the concern that is running the ferry or from those who use the ferry and the wharf. It could be collected by the ferry man and turned over to the government. The minister takes my remarks in a wholly wrong spirit. I prefaced what I said a moment ago with the observation that I knew this was a growth over a long period of years, and I suggested it was time-

Supply-Harbours and Rivers
I made the same suggestion last year-that we paused to consider either making these services revenue-producing and self-sustaining, or else stopping the expenditure. Now, it must be impressed upon the minds of all, and I am sure if the government can for one moment get away from the political aspect of it they must be impressed too, that tremendous pressure is being brought to bear for new wharves. Look at the wharves we discussed this afternoon-some of them utterly unnecessary. Again I cite what my right hon. leader stated-an expenditure of $78,000 in a con-stituensy where there has been nothing spent for some years, showing there was no need for an annual expenditure as indicated. And so it goes on in these dayi when everyone is anxious to curtail public undertakings. But when we come to the minister with a desire to discuss the matter fairly and non-politically, he comes back with a quasi-political speech. I again say to the minister that when out of public moneys we oan spend $16,000 on a wharf for a ferry to land at, it is time we collected some revenue to make that a selfsustaining service.

Mr. Chairman, I would submit that a wharf of this kind should be a provincial undertaking entirely. I cannot see any difference betweeen this and furnishing a ferry service, say, across some of the rivers in the prairie provinces which the municipalities and the provincial government have themselves to provide. For instance, there are places in my own constituency where the farmers cannot even market their grain until the rivers are frozen over. Pocketed in certain places as they'- are, they can get no help either from the government or the Canadian National Railways to build them a railway. But I cannot see why those people there should be taxed to construct works here, which are simply provincial and municipal in character, while they have to fight their own battles. When a short while ago the member for Springfield (Mr. Hoey) asked the question, the minister took the ground that the municipalities in the case that the member brought forward should look after themselves. I submit that most of the votes we have passed to-night are for municipal or provincial undertakings, and these should not come under the care of the [DOT]Dominion government at all.
Is the wharf built at the request of the ferry company, which I understand is a steamship company?

No, the wharf is for general use. It so happens there is a service between Pembroke and Desjardins, the
former being the trading town of the people in this district.
There is no business for the wharf except what the ferry brings.

They transact
other business on the river.

I do not know what
it would be.
Is it a floating wharf?

No, it is a
permanent wharf.

Item agreed to.
Doucet's Landing (Ste. Angele de Laval)-dredging, $25,000.
Where is that?
Nicolet county.
Has there been dredging done in previous years?
Yes.
How deep are they trying to make the water there?

Twelve feet at
low water level.
Will this complete the programme?

It will complete
the dredging programme, yes.

St. Lawrence dredging
does not usually appear in these votes. This must be some localized dredging.

This is just in
front of Three Rivers. It is the south end of the ferry between Three Rivers and the south shore. Dredging is done from time to time in order that the service may be carried on. With regard to dredging on the St. Lawrence, the Department of Public Works do a very considerable amount of dredging.
Not under these separate votes.

Yes, if they are
large enough they are put in a separate vote.
Is any company especially to get the benefit of this?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext:
Canadian National
Railways. There is a branch line from Arthabaska to this place, communicating with Three Rivers. It was a branch line of the old Grand Trunk. Doucet's Landing is on the south shore; Three Rivers is on the north shore.

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

How much was spent
there last year?
Nothing last year.

When was the dredging
done there before?
Altogether $24,000 has been spent there in dredging.

At a place where only
that amount has been spent since confederation, why is it -that we need $2S,000 this year?

Dredging was
done some years ago and is now needed again. These places fill up and require dredging from time to time.

Has the Canadian
National Railways asked for this, or is it the member for the riding thinks it would be a good thing?
The Deputy Minister of Railways asked for it.

But not the National
Railways?
Yes, the National Railways.

Who wrote on their
behalf?

The Deputy Minister of Railway and Canals wrote in 1924 asking whether the department would consider taking over this wharf and enlarge and repair same; also some dredging. The engineer recommends the work. Estimated cost, $24,786 for dredging and $213 for inspection fees.

There was no request
there by the National Railways to do dredging. There was a letter from the deputy minister wanting to know if the Department of Public Works would take over the wharf. That is not a request from the National Railways to do dredging.

I imagine he
was acting on behalf of the railways. He is a director of the railways. All the requests from the Canadian National Railways come through that office.
He is also Deputy Minister of Railways, and he may have been asking on their account. But anyway he did not ask for the dredging; what he asked for was the taking over of the wharf.
Wharf and dredging.

Who did the dredging
before?
The Public Works department.

Then you would not
take over the dredging. I did not catch any dredging in the letter.

I did not read
any letter; I simply referred to the notes here. It is stated that the deputy minister in 1924 asked the department if they would consider taking over the wharf, repair same and provide for dredging. There is nothing unusual about that. It seems to me it would be the proper channel through which the request should come.

I would not think that
would be the way at all. If the National Railways made a request for a certain expenditure they would probably make it through the Railway department, who would transmit the request to the Public AVorks department. What the minister has given us is merely a request from one department to take over a certain wharf, or the responsibility for it, and do some dredging for the other department, that is all.
That is all.
So then we have nothing in the way of a request from the National Railways.
It is not essential that there should be.

I did not say it was,
but I asked if there was, and the answer now is exactly opposite to that first given. It is really the member for the riding who thinks it would help out a little, I guess.

All right. This
